what: Local Pooled Error-Based ANOVA for RNA-Seq Count Data
title: Local Pooled Error-Based ANOVA for RNA-Seq Count Data
text: LPEseq2 R package differential expression analysis RNA-seq count data using local pooled error-based ANOVA conventional ANOVA, supporting one-way multi-way (interaction-free) designs. RNA-seq experiments controlled model systems — cell lines, organoids animal models, well pilot experiments — often limited one two replicates per condition repeated assays costly material scarce. constraint especially common single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq), high per-sample cost library preparation sequencing often restricts number biological donors one two per condition, even large numbers cells profiled. low-replicate conditions, conventional differential expression methods DESeq2 edgeR may produce unreliable results fail run, per-gene dispersion estimation becomes unstable. LPEseq2 addresses borrowing variance information across genes similar expression intensities rather estimating per gene independently, making applicable even one replicate per group available. variance modelled function expression intensity, LPEseq2 best suited controlled experiments; less suited heterogeneous samples, human tissue cohorts, inter-individual variability main question. LPEseq2 supports LPE-ANOVA small-sample RNA-seq data, standard gene-wise ANOVA larger sample sizes, automatic mode selects analysis method based group sample size. design can one-way (~ group) multi-way multiple main-effect factors interaction terms (~ genotype + treatment); see Multi-way (-interaction) designs. LPEseq2 also provides Seurat-integrated pseudo-bulk workflow cell-type-resolved differential expression analysis annotated scRNA-seq data. particularly useful number biological donors per condition small conventional pseudo-bulk methods. LPEseq2 intended complementary exploratory tool, replacement established methods DESeq2, edgeR, limma-voom adequate replication available. p-values adjusted p-values produced LPEseq2 treated approximate candidate-gene ranking measures rather calibrated false discovery rate guarantees. Biological follow-validation recommended. can also run LPEseq2 directly browser without installation: Launch LPEseq2 Shiny Web Tool

Counts must non-negative free NA/Inf. column names count matrix row names colData must contain sample names (order may differ; colData reordered match count matrix). count table stored text file can read format, example: Shiny web tool accepts CSV, TSV, delimiter-separated text files (.txt) directly; , first column must contain gene identifiers, separator detected automatically. what: Seurat object input for pseudo-bulk analysis
title: Local Pooled Error-Based ANOVA for RNA-Seq Count Data
text: pseudo-bulk analysis, input annotated Seurat object raw counts cell-level metadata. Seurat object contain metadata columns sample ID, condition, cell type annotation. metadata column names can customized using sample_col, condition_col, celltype_col arguments. Pseudo-bulk count matrices generated summing raw counts across cells within sample cell type. Normalized log-normalized expression values used pseudo-bulk aggregation. Pseudo-bulk samples built fewer min_cells cells (default 10) removed. LPE_pseudobulk(), cell type analysed one-way design condition column (~ condition); multi-way designs variance.eval available LPE_preprocess() + LPE_ANOVA(). Two aggregation modes supported:
code: seurat_obj$sample_id seurat_obj$condition seurat_obj$celltype

title: Local Pooled Error-Based ANOVA for RNA-Seq Count Data
text: cell numbers substantially unequal across samples within cell type, normalize_by_ncells option can used reduce imbalance. normalize_by_ncells = TRUE, sample’s aggregated count vector scaled per-ncells_scale-cells basis. equivalent computing CP1K (Counts per 1K Cells) ncells_scale = 1000 (default): equalizes contribution sample regardless cell count, particularly important rare cell types cell counts differ markedly across samples. Normalization method compatibility: normalize_by_ncells = TRUE produces non-integer values. Therefore, TMM DESeq2 normalization automatically disabled require raw integer counts: normalize.method "TMM" (LPE_pseudobulk() default) "DESeq2", set "none" warning. library_size normalization remains available can combined normalize_by_ncells = TRUE additionally correct sequencing depth differences cell-number scaling: normalize_by_ncells = TRUE normalize.method = "none" (explicitly, TMM/DESeq2 switched ), cell-number imbalance corrected. Sequencing depth differences remain uncorrected. min.count threshold adjusted match scaled count values (example, min.count = 1 instead default 5).
code: CP1K = (sum of raw counts across cells) / n_cells × 1000      = raw_count / (n_cells / ncells_scale) # Correct for both cell-number imbalance and sequencing depth res_pb <- LPE_pseudobulk(   seurat_obj = seurat_obj,   method = "sample",   normalize_by_ncells = TRUE,   ncells_scale = 1000,   normalize.method = "library_size",   # additionally correct for sequencing depth   min.count = 1,   sample_col = "sample_id",   condition_col = "condition",   celltype_col = "celltype" )

title: Local Pooled Error-Based ANOVA for RNA-Seq Count Data
text: every group least two samples, automatic rule trains variance trend within-group replicate pairs , without trimming (see Automatic variance-training settings).
code: library(LPEseq2)  set.seed(123)  # 1,000 genes x 6 samples (3 Control, 3 Treatment) counts <- matrix(   rnbinom(6000, mu = 50, size = 10),   nrow = 1000,   ncol = 6 )  rownames(counts) <- paste0("gene", 1:1000) colnames(counts) <- paste0("sample", 1:6)  colData <- data.frame(   group = rep(c("Control", "Treatment"), each = 3),   row.names = colnames(counts) )  prep <- LPE_preprocess(   counts = counts,   colData = colData,   design = ~ group,   normalize.method = "library_size",   # default   verbose = FALSE )  # Default settings: analysis.method = "LPE", # trim.method = "auto", use_weighted_between = "auto", # n.bin = 100, df = 10, p.method = "chisq" res <- LPE_ANOVA(object = prep, verbose = FALSE)  head(res) attr(res, "analysis.method")            # "LPE" attr(res, "variance.settings")$rule #> "within-group (replicate) pairs only, no trimming (smallest cell n = 3)"

what: Example with the bundled test data
title: Local Pooled Error-Based ANOVA for RNA-Seq Count Data
text: package ships simulated test data results expected current version inst/testdat/: comparison run automatically package tests (tests/testthat/test-expected-results.R).
code: library(LPEseq2)  testdat <- system.file("testdat", package = "LPEseq2") read_counts <- function(f) as.matrix(read.csv(file.path(testdat, f),                                               row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)) read_meta <- function(f) read.csv(file.path(testdat, f), row.names = 1)  # Two groups, ~ group prep2 <- LPE_preprocess(read_counts("LPEseq2_2group_test_counts.csv"),                         read_meta("LPEseq2_2group_test_metadata.csv"),                         design = ~ group, verbose = FALSE) res2 <- LPE_ANOVA(prep2, verbose = FALSE) sum(res2$q.value < 0.05) #> 82  # Three groups with a batch factor, ~ group + batch prep3 <- LPE_preprocess(read_counts("LPEseq2_test_counts.csv"),                         read_meta("LPEseq2_test_metadata.csv"),                         design = ~ group + batch, verbose = FALSE) res3 <- LPE_ANOVA(prep3, verbose = FALSE) sum(res3$q.value_group < 0.05) #> 133 sum(res3$q.value_batch < 0.05) #> 3  # Compare with the shipped expected results expected <- read.csv(file.path(testdat, "LPEseq2_2group_expected_results.csv")) all.equal(res2$p.value, expected$p.value) #> TRUE

what: Pseudo-bulk analysis from an annotated Seurat object
title: Local Pooled Error-Based ANOVA for RNA-Seq Count Data
text: recommended pseudo-bulk workflow aggregate raw counts sample--cell-type level run LPEseq2 separately cell type. analysis.method = "auto", standard ANOVA used cell type every condition least standard.min.group.n pseudo-bulk samples; otherwise LPE-ANOVA used. method variance-training rule chosen cell type reported selected_LPEseq2_method variance_training columns result. cell numbers substantially unequal across samples within cell type, use normalize_by_ncells = TRUE scale sample’s counts CP1K (per-1000-cells) basis analysis: Note: normalize_by_ncells = TRUE, TMM DESeq2 normalization automatically disabled require raw integer counts. Use normalize.method = "library_size" "none" combination normalize_by_ncells = TRUE. combined result across analyzed cell types can accessed : Cell-type-specific results can accessed : Pseudo-bulk metadata diagnostic information can checked : selected cell types analyzed, use celltypes argument:
code: library(LPEseq2)  # Standard pseudo-bulk (raw integer counts) # Defaults shown: normalize.method = "TMM" (requires edgeR), # analysis.method = "auto", trim.method = "auto", use_weighted_between = "auto" res_pb <- LPE_pseudobulk(   seurat_obj = seurat_obj,   method = "sample",   assay = "RNA",   counts_layer = "counts",   sample_col = "sample_id",   condition_col = "condition",   celltype_col = "celltype",   min_cells = 10,   normalize.method = "TMM",   analysis.method = "auto",   standard.min.group.n = 5,   p.method = "chisq",   verbose = TRUE ) # Cell-number-normalized pseudo-bulk (CP1K scaling) res_pb_norm <- LPE_pseudobulk(   seurat_obj = seurat_obj,   method = "sample",   assay = "RNA",   counts_layer = "counts",   sample_col = "sample_id",   condition_col = "condition",   celltype_col = "celltype",   min_cells = 10,   normalize_by_ncells = TRUE,       # scale to CP1K (per-1000-cells) basis   ncells_scale = 1000,   normalize.method = "library_size", # additionally correct for sequencing depth   min.count = 1,                     # adjust threshold for scaled count values   analysis.method = "auto",   standard.min.group.n = 5,   p.method = "chisq",   verbose = TRUE ) all_res <- res_pb$combined_result head(all_res) names(res_pb$results_by_celltype)  cd4_res <- res_pb$results_by_celltype$CD4_T head(cd4_res) cd4_meta <- res_pb$metadata_by_celltype$CD4_T head(cd4_meta)  res_pb$diagnostics$CD4_T res_pb$errors res_cd4 <- LPE_pseudobulk(   seurat_obj = seurat_obj,   method = "sample",   celltypes = c("CD4_T"),   sample_col = "sample_id",   condition_col = "condition",   celltype_col = "celltype" )

title: Local Pooled Error-Based ANOVA for RNA-Seq Count Data
text: iqr trimming method applies conventional 1.5 × IQR boxplot rule within expression-intensity -bins. use_weighted_between = TRUE, within-group -group-derived pairwise values pooled trimming; outliers detected M-value scale used variance trend estimation. Explicitly supplied values override automatic rule. example (three samples per group), automatic rule use replicate pairs without trimming; setting arguments forces -group pairs IQR trimming.

title: Local Pooled Error-Based ANOVA for RNA-Seq Count Data
text: design LPE_preprocess() accepts one main-effect term, e.g. ~ genotype + treatment. Interaction terms (:B *B) supported raise error, since LPE variance-trend / test-statistic machinery assumes additive model. design term’s main effect tested Type II sum--squares decomposition (comparing full additive model model term dropped), order-independent main-effects-design. one-way design, result columns unsuffixed (MS_between, F, p.value, q.value, …) exactly . multi-way design, one set columns reported per term, suffixed term name, e.g.: analysis.method = "standard_anova", MS_within df2 reported df1_<term> added term. variance.eval = "per_group" (Welch-style, per-group variance evaluation) supported one-way designs; raises error multi-way designs; use variance.eval = "grand_mean" (default) instead. attr(res, "design.terms") reports design term names tested. Column names syntactically valid R names (example time point, containing space) can used design backquoted, e.g. ~ genotype + `time point`; output columns named F_time point, q.value_time point, .
code: set.seed(1)  # 1,000 genes x 8 samples: 2 genotypes x 2 treatments, 2 samples per combination counts_mw <- matrix(   rnbinom(8000, mu = 50, size = 10),   nrow = 1000,   ncol = 8,   dimnames = list(paste0("gene", 1:1000), paste0("s", 1:8)) )  colData_mw <- data.frame(   genotype  = rep(rep(c("wt", "mut"), each = 2), times = 2),   treatment = rep(c("control", "drug"), each = 4),   row.names = colnames(counts_mw) )  prep_mw <- LPE_preprocess(   counts = counts_mw,   colData = colData_mw,   design = ~ genotype + treatment,   normalize.method = "library_size",   verbose = FALSE )  res_mw <- LPE_ANOVA(   object = prep_mw,   analysis.method = "auto",   standard.min.group.n = 5,   verbose = FALSE )  head(res_mw) attr(res_mw, "analysis.method")   # "LPE" (2 samples per combination < 5) attr(res_mw, "design.terms")      # "genotype" "treatment" gene, mean, var, MS_between_genotype, F_genotype, p.value_genotype, q.value_genotype, MS_between_treatment, F_treatment, p.value_treatment, q.value_treatment, method

title: Local Pooled Error-Based ANOVA for RNA-Seq Count Data
text: defaults trim.method = "auto" use_weighted_between = "auto", LPE_ANOVA() LPE_pseudobulk() choose pairwise values train variance trend replication design cells (unique combinations design factor levels): Replicate pairs contain treatment effect, trimming removes genuine noise -estimates variance (liberal calls); -group pairs contain true effects must trimmed. rule follows LPEseq1 (Gim et al. 2016), uses replicate pairs without outlier removal whenever group replicated, trimmed -condition pairs non-replicated groups. Values given explicitly always used given. settings actually used stored attr(res, "variance.settings") (variance_training column LPE_pseudobulk() results). attr(res, "variance.settings") also contains trim.method, use_weighted_between, auto (whether automatic rule applied), replicated, min_cell_n, variance.trend ("pooled" "per_group"), , variance.eval = "per_group", trend.source (trend used group).

title: Local Pooled Error-Based ANOVA for RNA-Seq Count Data
text: LPEseq2 supports IQR-based fixed-threshold (dvalue) outlier trimming pairwise values used variance trend estimation. default trim.method = "auto" selects "none" "dvalue" described Automatic variance-training settings. trim.method = "iqr", LPEseq2 first collects training values (within-group pairwise values, plus -group-derived values use_weighted_between = TRUE). values divided expression-intensity -bins, conventional boxplot rule applied within bin: trim.method = "dvalue", LPEseq2 removes pairwise value whose M value (rescaled difference used variance estimation) exceeds d.threshold / sqrt(2) absolute value, prior variance trend estimation. Thresholding M rather raw D keeps cutoff equally strict regardless within- vs. -group origin group size. reproduces outlier-removal step LPEseq1’s non-replicate analysis (Gim et al. 2016), equivalent M value thresholded fixed value (default d.threshold = 1.2, .e. |M| ≤ 0.849) chosen empirically via reproducibility analysis across benchmark datasets. Users verify whether default appropriate normalization scale log-transform. Outlier detection performed M-value scale M scale used local pooled variance estimation.
code: lower_bound = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR upper_bound = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR

One "auto" (default), "dvalue", "iqr", "none". "auto" chooses replication (see Automatic variance-training settings Details): "none" every design cell least two samples, otherwise "dvalue". See LPE_ANOVA_var trimming rules. use_weighted_between "auto" (default), TRUE FALSE. Whether include weighted -group differences variance trend estimation. "auto" uses FALSE every design cell least two samples (replicate pairs ), otherwise TRUE. d.threshold Numeric. Threshold LPEseq1 raw-D scale, used derive fixed M-scale cutoff (d.threshold/sqrt(2)) applied trim.method = "dvalue". Default 1.2, matching default reported LPEseq1 (Gim et al. 2016). Ignored trim.method values. See LPE_ANOVA_var details. analysis.method Analysis method. One "LPE", "standard_anova", "auto". "LPE" uses local pooled error-based ANOVA. "standard_anova" uses conventional gene-wise ANOVA (Type II sums squares multi-way designs). "auto" selects standard ANOVA every factor-level combination (design "cell") least standard.min.group.n samples; otherwise, LPE-ANOVA used. standard.min.group.n Minimum per-cell sample size required use standard ANOVA analysis.method = "auto". "cell" unique combination design factor levels (one-way design, simply group). verbose Logical. Whether print progress messages. p.method P-value calculation method. One "chisq" "F_inf". variance.eval Character string specifying fitted variance trend evaluated test statistic. One "grand_mean" "per_group". "grand_mean" (default) evaluates variance trend gene's overall (grand) mean expression uses single pooled variance test statistic; mode supports one-way multi-way (main-effects-) designs. "per_group" evaluates variance trend separately group's mean expression combines group-specific variances via inverse-variance weighting Welch-type unequal-variance test statistic (returned method = "LPE_Welch" different var/MS_between definition; see Details). "per_group" supported one-way designs (single design term); raises error multi-way designs. variance.trend Character string specifying variance trend read group variance.eval = "per_group". One "pooled" (default) "per_group". "pooled" reads every group's variance single trend estimated design cells (behaviour previous versions). "per_group" fits separate variance trend every group least two samples, using group's replicate pairs, LPEseq1 original LPE method; groups single sample read variance pooled trend. used variance.eval = "per_group"; requesting "per_group" together variance.eval = "grand_mean" raises error. See Details.

title: Run LPE-ANOVA — LPE_ANOVA
code: testdat <- system.file("testdat", package = "LPEseq2") read_counts <- function(f) as.matrix(read.csv(file.path(testdat, f),                                               row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)) read_meta <- function(f) read.csv(file.path(testdat, f), row.names = 1)  ## Two groups (6 vs 6), one-way design prep2 <- LPE_preprocess(read_counts("LPEseq2_2group_test_counts.csv"),                         read_meta("LPEseq2_2group_test_metadata.csv"),                         design = ~ group, verbose = FALSE) res2 <- LPE_ANOVA(prep2, verbose = FALSE) head(res2[order(res2$p.value), ]) #>         gene     mean       var MS_between        F      p.value      q.value #> 12 gene_0012 7.073082 0.2899427   18.05682 62.27719 2.983604e-15 2.983604e-12 #> 19 gene_0019 7.802183 0.2598390   13.35244 51.38738 7.582448e-13 3.791224e-10 #> 38 gene_0038 7.117452 0.2878370   14.11076 49.02344 2.529213e-12 8.430709e-10 #> 22 gene_0022 7.010981 0.2934340   13.66770 46.57846 8.802260e-12 2.200565e-09 #> 11 gene_0011 7.820358 0.2589403   11.78999 45.53169 1.501890e-11 3.003780e-09 #> 24 gene_0024 7.448984 0.2759103   10.95124 39.69129 2.974497e-10 4.957495e-08 #>    method #> 12    LPE #> 19    LPE #> 38    LPE #> 22    LPE #> 11    LPE #> 24    LPE sum(res2$q.value < 0.05) #> [1] 82 attr(res2, "variance.settings")$rule #> [1] "within-group (replicate) pairs only, no trimming (smallest cell n = 6)"  ## Welch-type statistic with group-specific variance trends res2_pg <- LPE_ANOVA(prep2, variance.eval = "per_group",                      variance.trend = "per_group", verbose = FALSE) attr(res2_pg, "variance.settings")$trend.source #>     Control Treatment_A  #>       "own"       "own"   ## Three groups with a batch factor, additive design ~ group + batch prep3 <- LPE_preprocess(read_counts("LPEseq2_test_counts.csv"),                         read_meta("LPEseq2_test_metadata.csv"),                         design = ~ group + batch, verbose = FALSE) res3 <- LPE_ANOVA(prep3, verbose = FALSE) head(res3[order(res3$p.value_group), ]) #>         gene     mean       var MS_between_group  F_group p.value_group #> 11 gene_0011 7.383532 0.2868123         9.580432 33.40314  3.113159e-15 #> 12 gene_0012 6.888715 0.3068180         9.391096 30.60804  5.094461e-14 #> 38 gene_0038 6.802491 0.3119396         8.997715 28.84442  2.971858e-13 #> 19 gene_0019 7.543674 0.2804833         7.886401 28.11719  6.149783e-13 #> 22 gene_0022 6.711890 0.3181820         8.593651 27.00860  1.863438e-12 #> 25 gene_0025 8.482922 0.2395040         6.363551 26.56971  2.890156e-12 #>    q.value_group MS_between_batch    F_batch p.value_batch q.value_batch method #> 11  3.113159e-12       0.21966581 0.76588690    0.38149249     0.9983678    LPE #> 12  2.547231e-11       0.02524831 0.08229086    0.77421659     0.9983678    LPE #> 38  9.906192e-11       0.07251272 0.23245758    0.62970753     0.9983678    LPE #> 19  1.537446e-10       0.10840430 0.38649114    0.53414960     0.9983678    LPE #> 22  3.726877e-10       0.07196450 0.22617398    0.63437539     0.9983678    LPE #> 25  4.816926e-10       0.75357457 3.14639711    0.07609481     0.7939179    LPE  ## title: Estimate Intensity-Dependent Variance Trend for LPE-ANOVA — LPE_ANOVA_var
text: function estimates intensity-dependent variance trend using within-group pairwise differences. Following LPEseq1 (Gim et al. 2016), raw pairwise difference D symmetrized \(\pm D\) quantile binning, pooled difference distribution used variance estimation centered zero construction rather subtracting empirically estimated mean. Optionally, weighted -group differences can included replicate information limited. trimming enabled, conventional 1.5*IQR rule applied within expression-intensity bins pairwise values used variance trend estimation.

One "iqr", "dvalue", "none". "iqr" applies conventional 1.5*IQR boxplot rule within expression-intensity -bins pooling within-group -group values. "dvalue" applies fixed threshold M value (rescaled pairwise difference actually used variance estimation), converted d.threshold d.threshold/sqrt(2), LPEseq1's non-replicate outlier procedure (Gim et al. 2016): pairwise value |M| greater converted threshold removed, independent bin group size. "none" performs outlier trimming. use_weighted_between Logical. Whether include weighted -group differences variance trend estimation. d.threshold Numeric. Threshold LPEseq1 raw-D scale, used derive fixed M-scale cutoff (d.threshold/sqrt(2)) applied trim.method = "dvalue". Default 1.2, matching default reported LPEseq1 (Gim et al. 2016). Ignored trim.method values. See LPE_ANOVA_var details.

title: Estimate Intensity-Dependent Variance Trend for LPE-ANOVA — LPE_ANOVA_var

Consequently, pairwise counts reported returned trim.info (e.g. n_total_before, n_within_before, n_between_before, _after/_removed counterparts) twice number underlying replicate/group pairs.

title: LPEseq2 0.1.1
text: package now ships results expected bundled test data (inst/testdat/LPEseq2_2group_expected_results.csv, inst/testdat/LPEseq2_multiway_expected_results.csv) script regenerates (inst/testdat/make_expected_results.R); new test (test-expected-results.R) checks current code reproduces . LPE_preprocess(), LPE_ANOVA() LPE_ANOVA_var() gained runnable examples based bundled test data. LPE_pseudobulk(): removed redundant checks package make_pseudobulk_from_seurat(). DESCRIPTION: authors (ORCID) package description updated. Shiny app: removed commented-volcano plot code. LPE_ANOVA(): new argument variance.trend = c("pooled", "per_group"), used variance.eval = "per_group" (one-way designs). "per_group", every group least two samples reads variance trend, fitted group’s replicate pairs (trimming trim.method = "auto"; explicit trim.method applied given), LPEseq1 original LPE method replicated conditions. Single-sample groups use pooled trend, LPEseq1 non-replicated conditions; group whose trend fitted falls back pooled trend warning. Welch-type test statistic unchanged. default "pooled" keeps previous results identical (also variance.eval = "grand_mean" multi-way designs). Requesting variance.trend = "per_group" variance.eval = "grand_mean" raises error. group-specific trends returned attr(res, "var.spline.group") attr(res, "base.var.group"); attr(res, "variance.settings") gains variance.trend trend.source (trend used group). LPE_ANOVA_var(): accepts single group least two samples use_weighted_between = FALSE (needed group-specific trends).

title: LPEseq2 0.1.0
text: LPE_ANOVA() / LPE_pseudobulk(): new default trim.method = "auto" use_weighted_between = "auto". variance-training pairs chosen replication design cells: every cell least two samples, within-cell replicate pairs used, without trimming (use_weighted_between = FALSE, trim.method = "none"); cell single sample, weighted -group pairs added D-value trimming applied (TRUE, "dvalue", previous default). follows LPEseq1, uses replicate pairs without outlier removal replicated groups. simulations cell-line-like data, trimming replicate pairs -estimated variance (mean FDR 0.12 nominal 0.05 two three replicates), replicate pairs without trimming kept FDR closer nominal (0.075) similar F1. Results replicates every group differ version 0.0.1 defaults used. reproduce 0.0.1, set trim.method = "dvalue", use_weighted_between = TRUE. Explicitly supplied values used unchanged. settings actually used returned attr(res, "variance.settings") (trim.method, use_weighted_between, auto, replicated, min_cell_n, rule); LPE_pseudobulk() adds variance_training column per cell type. Shiny web tool: “Pairwise outlier trimming method” “Use weighted -group differences” offer “Auto replication (recommended)” default (latter now drop-instead check box). resolved setting shown Method info written downloaded results (variance_training column).

title: LPEseq2 0.0.1
text: Shiny web tool (app.R): single “Group variable” dropdown replaced dynamic set dropdowns controlled “+” / “-” buttons, several testing-group factors can added design (~ + B + ..., interaction). Selections preserved factor added, new dropdown defaults first unused metadata column, duplicate / NA / single-level selections give clear message, “Variance evaluation” restricted grand_mean one factor chosen. design formula built backquoted names, metadata columns containing spaces now work (also one-way analyses). LPE_preprocess() / LPE_ANOVA() / standard_ANOVA_expr(): design variables non-syntactic names (e.g. time point) supported multi-way formulas via backquotes; output columns use plain name (F_time point). LPE_preprocess() / LPE_ANOVA() / standard_ANOVA_expr(): added support multi-way (main-effects-) designs. design can now formula one term, e.g. ~ genotype + treatment, addition one-way ~ group. Interaction terms (:B *B) supported raise error, since LPE variance-trend / test-statistic machinery assumes additive model. design term’s main effect tested via Type II sum--squares decomposition (RSS model term dropped, minus RSS full model), order-independent additive design reduces exactly original one-way computation single term (verified numerically identical). one-way design, LPE_ANOVA() output columns unchanged (MS_between, F, p.value, q.value, …); multi-way design, one suffixed set columns reported per design term (e.g. F_genotype, p.value_genotype, F_treatment, p.value_treatment, …). LPE_preprocess()’s returned list gains factors field (named list individual design factors); group kept backward compatibility now represents crossing design factors (identical single factor one-way designs). variance.eval = "per_group" (Welch-style) remains one-way raises informative error multi-way designs; analysis.method = "auto" now bases group-size check minimum factor-level combination (“cell”) size. LPE_ANOVA_var() unchanged. LPE_ANOVA_var(): pairwise D/M values used intensity-dependent variance trend estimation now symmetrized ±D trimming quantile binning, matching LPEseq1’s original approach (Gim et al. 2016) fixing difference distribution’s center zero. changes variance estimation formula data-estimated-mean variance known-mean (zero) variance, shift var, F, p.value, q.value LPE_ANOVA() results (LPE-ANOVA mode) compared previous versions. trim.info pairwise counts (n_total_before, n_within_before, n_between_before, _after/_removed counterparts) now twice number underlying pairs. LPE_pseudobulk() now supports trim.method = "dvalue" d.threshold argument, matching LPE_ANOVA() / LPE_ANOVA_var(). Previously "iqr" "none" available pseudobulk level even though "dvalue" already implemented underlying LPE_ANOVA_var(). LPE_ANOVA() / LPE_ANOVA_var() / LPE_pseudobulk(): trim.method default changed "iqr" "dvalue". LPE_ANOVA() / LPE_ANOVA_var() / LPE_pseudobulk(): use_weighted_between default changed FALSE TRUE. LPE_ANOVA() gained variance.eval argument ("grand_mean" (default) "per_group"), controlling whether intensity-dependent variance evaluated grand mean separately per group (Welch-style, equivalent LPEseq1’s Z-test k = 2). LPE_ANOVA_var(): trim.method = "dvalue" now applies threshold M scale (d.threshold / sqrt(2)) instead raw D scale. previous raw-D thresholding, effective strictness outlier removal -group pairs became lenient group sample size increased; thresholding M keeps cutoff equally strict regardless group size, numerically identical previous behavior groups exactly one sample (LPEseq1’s original design).
